newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips close up on heavy foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips close up on heavy foreign buying.

text.p: Aggressive buying of leading Malaysian stocks by foreign institutional funds pushed the market to a higher close, market players said.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 1.25 percent or 14.00 points to 1131.55, while the all-share EMAS Index closed up 5.50 points at 329.70.
Ami Moris, vice president of dealing at Capitalcorp Securities said: "All the indicators are pointing to a break-out of the recent range-bound trading activity."
She attributed the surge on the local bourse to British and Japanese institutional funds actively buying Malaysian stocks.
Moris pointed to political and economic uncertainties in neighbouring Thailand and Indonesia as factors that induced the inflow of foreign funds into Malaysia.
Dealers said regional markets also rallied on the abatement of fears over inlfationary pressures in the U.S. economy.
Diversified stockbroking firm Rashid Hussain rose to a new high for the year, closing up 50 cents at 12.10 ringgit on speculation of a group restructuring.
Property developer Khong Guan was the most actively traded, rising 5.30 ringgit at 27.00 ringgit on speculative buying, with 14.6 million shares traded.
